gate_multiplier_robustness.note: Task statement uses the panel task field 1.0; MEMORY/docs/task222-gate-v8.md says the panel multipliers are initial values (day 0.75-2.0) and production continues staircase. The new block is slightly further from gate under both definitions.

conclusion.headline: Day regression decomposes into roughly equal data and fine-tune halves. r108 A (same data, from scratch) loses 7.6pp on the day panel; r108 B (from r101) loses another 7.6pp. The data effect is task-specific (L6/L8/L9 collapse in both A and B; L9 is 0/23 for both vs 13/23 incumbent), while the fine-tune effect is task-specific elsewhere (B collapses L4 5/23 vs A 20/23, L2 14/23 vs A 21/23).
data_side: All +554,820 day rows are teacher_line; existing day sources (llm_demo 1,388,668; teacher_r52 1,191,050) are unchanged.
The new day block is bimodal: 43.4% is >=1.75x and 27.3% is <1.0x; only 27.4% is exactly 1.0x. Old day was 21.7% >=1.75x, 7.5% <1.0x and 66.8% exactly 1.0x.

92.9% of the new block is perturb-family; only 2.6% (14,415 rows) matches a gate day deck, all of them one deck at L8, and only 2,659 of those are at exactly 1.0 (the rest are 0.5/0.75). Seven of the eight gate day levels get zero new gate-deck rows.
The new block is 63.2% prior r101, 25.7% r95, 11.1% r94; 37.5% is the Mac197 batch and 36.7% is the rd193 task family.
A and B both collapse on L8 (3/23, 2/23 vs 13/23) and L9 (0/23, 0/23 vs 13/23); A also drops L6 (3 vs 9), so the new block at those levels is the leading data-side suspect, not merely fine-tuning.

The data effect is a reshuffle, not a uniform loss: A gains L2 (+8) and L4 (+10) over incumbent but loses L6 (-6), L8 (-10) and L9 (-13). The near-flat A day average (+18 on L2/L4 offsets -29 on L6/L8/L9) hides this task-level swap.
finetune_side: r108 A (same data, gptbc_s1 init, 8ep, lr 0.002) day panel 44.0%; r108 B (r101 init, 4ep, lr 0.0005) 36.4%; incumbent 51.6%.

B is much worse than A specifically on L4 (5 vs 20 wins) and L2 (14 vs 21), while A is close to or above incumbent there. The L4/L2 data cannot be intrinsically poisonous because A trains on the same rows and succeeds.
B gains over A on L3 (+5), L6 (+3), L7 (+2), and on pool (+14.1pp) and night (+7.6pp); the fine-tune is trading day/fog/roof for pool/night, not uniformly degrading.
r107 B at lr 0.002 had a larger day drop than r108 B at lr 0.0005, consistent with an lr/update-budget dose-response.
conclusion.most_likely: Two mechanisms, roughly half each: (1) data-side — the new teacher_line day block is 43% >=1.75x and 27% <1.0x (only 27% exactly 1.0x) perturb, and adds no gate-deck rows at 7 of 8 gate levels, and both A and B collapse on L8/L9; (2) fine-tune-side — 4 epochs at lr 5e-4 from r101 overwrites the r101-specific L4/L2 day policy, which A from scratch retains. The aggregate day drop is not one homogeneous cause.
caveats: The evaluation.log look 2 uses 23 pairs per panel task (184 day pairs), not the 280-pair gate table; rates are consistent with the table (B 36.4% vs 34.3%, incumbent 51.6% vs 50.7%), so the task pattern is usable but the absolute counts differ.

Gate multipliers: the task statement says 1.0, matching the panel task field, but MEMORY/docs/task222-gate-v8.md says the panel multipliers are initial values (day 0.75-2.0) and production continues staircase. gate_multiplier_robustness shows the new block is slightly further from gate under both definitions, so the direction of the conclusion does not depend on this choice.
A vs B also changes init and epochs, so the fine-tune half is not a pure lr estimate.
The 14,415 gate-deck rows (only 2,659 at exactly 1.0) are not the gate tasks themselves (different task ids/seeds), so no direct eval contamination.
Zone/family labels come from archive metadata; a few archives with missing task metadata are classified by background only.

experiments.change: Keep init/lr/epochs identical to r108 B, but remove (or downweight to 0.5) the new teacher_line day rows with multiplier >=1.75, especially the L6/L8/L9 cells; keep all other data unchanged.
experiments.expected: If the data-side diagnosis is right, L8/L9 recover toward incumbent (13/23 each) and L6 improves, while the B-specific L4/L2 collapse remains. Pool should stay clearly above r101 because its rows are untouched.
experiments.risk: Removing 240,875 rows (7.7% of day) changes total day volume and may hurt high-multiplier day generalization. If L8/L9 stay at 0-3/23, the cause is not the high-mult day block but the 1.0x new rows or the eval task mismatch.

experiments.change: Keep the exact r108 B data and 4 epochs, but retrain from r101 at lr 0.00025 instead of 0.0005. No other change.
experiments.expected: A clean lr ablation for the fine-tune half: L4 and L2 should recover at least toward r101 (10/23, 13/23), possibly toward A (20/23, 21/23), while L8/L9 stay low if they are data-driven. The pool gain should shrink but remain positive.
experiments.risk: Underfitting: pool/night gains may disappear and the run may not beat r101 anywhere. If L4/L2 do not recover, the fine-tune half is epoch/init-driven rather than lr-driven.
